channel.title: Ancient Intelligence
channel.description: Elias and Clara investigate the intelligence of the ancient world: mechanical computers, prediction engines, and knowledge systems built on a technological path we never went down, and ask whether reaching artificial intelligence is what ends civilizations. Evidence-anchored: what we know, what is claimed, what we wonder. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: The Pattern of the Fall
item.description:
The thesis episode: Atlantis as Plato actually told it, the Santorini eruption, Göbekli Tepe, the pyramid age, Puma Punku, and the Antikythera mechanism, and the question of whether reaching artificial intelligence is what ends civilizations.

item.title: The Antikythera Mechanism: The Computer That Should Not Exist
item.description:
A hand-cranked bronze computer from a Greek shipwreck: more than thirty gears predicting eclipses and tracking the Moon, a user manual in Greek, Cicero's accounts of similar machines, and the fourteen hundred years before anything like it existed again.

item.title: Göbekli Tepe: The Temple That Rewrote the Timeline
item.description:
Hunter-gatherers raised sixteen-ton carved pillars in southeastern Turkey eleven and a half thousand years ago, before farming, pottery, or writing, and then deliberately buried the place. Klaus Schmidt's discovery, his temple-first thesis, and what it does to the story of civilization.

item.title: Puma Punku: Machining Stone Before the Machine Age
item.description:
Elias and Clara at Puma Punku in Bolivia: the interlocking H blocks, the one hundred and thirty one ton red sandstone slab, the bronze cramps cast in place, Protzen and Nair on the finishing tools archaeology has never found, Posnansky and the seventeen thousand year claim, and the modular design system that died when Tiwanaku fell. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: The Baghdad Battery and the Technology of the Temple
item.description:
Elias and Clara on the Baghdad Battery: the fourteen centimetre terracotta jar from Khujut Rabu with its copper cylinder, iron rod and bitumen seal, Wilhelm König and the electroplating claim, Paul Keyser and the pain relief case, the Seleucia scroll vessels and the foundation ritual reading, and the looting of the Iraq Museum in two thousand and three that took the original with it. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: Oracles: The Original AI
item.description:
Elias and Clara on the oracles of the ancient world: the Pythia in the unseen adyton at Delphi, the four thousand lead tablets folded shut at Dodona, Alexander crossing the desert to Siwa in three hundred and thirty one before the common era, Croesus and his blind test of the oracles, the wooden walls debate that saved Athens at Salamis, the de Boer and Hale ethylene claim and its critics, Delphi as an information centre, and answers from a system no one fully understood. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: The Library of Ashurbanipal: The Knowledge That Burned
item.description:
Elias and Clara on the Library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh: more than thirty thousand clay tablets gathered by a literate king, the royal letter ordering Borsippa to hold nothing back, colophons and catalogues as ancient metadata, the omen series Enuma Anu Enlil, George Smith reading the Flood Tablet in eighteen seventy two, and the fire of six hundred and twelve before the common era that destroyed the boards and scrolls but baked the clay. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: Egypt's Granite Problem: Boxes, Vases, and Impossible Precision
item.description:
Elias and Clara on Egypt's granite problem: the twenty four Serapeum boxes at Saqqara, forty tonnes of Aswan granite polished flat in the dark, Christopher Dunn and his two ten thousandths of an inch, Denys Stocks drilling granite with copper and sand in twenty hours, predynastic stone vases under the scanner, the Petrie Museum study that concluded handmade, and whether measurement itself was the intelligence. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: The Quipu: The Empire That Computed in Knots
item.description:
Elias and Clara on the quipu: the knotted string computer of the Inca Empire, Locke and the decimal knots, the Puruchuco archive that sums like a spreadsheet, Urton and the binary code claim, Hyland and the Collata letters, the Santa Valley census match, and an archive whose key died with its keepers. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: Baalbek: The Stones Too Big to Move
item.description:
Elias and Clara at Baalbek in Lebanon: the Trilithon, three blocks of about eight hundred tonnes in the podium wall of the Temple of Jupiter, the thousand tonne Stone of the Pregnant Woman, the Forgotten Stone of sixteen hundred and fifty tonnes found in the quarry in two thousand and fourteen, Jean Pierre Adam and his capstan model, Graham Hancock and the twelve thousand year claim, and the organisational intelligence that moved mountains at walking pace. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: Sacsayhuaman: The Wall With No Blueprint
item.description:
Elias and Clara above Cusco, Peru: three zigzag walls of polygonal stone at Sacsayhuaman, blocks of about one hundred and twenty tonnes fitted without mortar or iron, Jean-Pierre Protzen and the trial and error method, the Killke layer beneath the Inca fortress, walls that rock and reseat through earthquakes, and the Spanish quarrying that left only the stones too heavy to steal. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence
